title: Inside Archive X: Unexplained Phenomena's UFO accounts - From encounters and alien abductions to prophetic dreams
excerpt: Archive X: Unexplained Phenomena will be the newest documentary series from AMC Global Media, with 6 episodes. The premiere will be on October 1, 2026, and viewers interested in all things UFO can watch it on SundanceTV.
content:
Alisha Khan

Updated Thu, September 17, 2026 at 11:26 AM UTC

Archive X: Unexplained Phenomena will be the newest documentary series from AMC Global Media, with 6 episodes. The premiere will be on October 1, 2026, and viewers interested in all things UFO can watch it on SundanceTV. It will also be available on AMC+ and All Reality each week.

The documentary is hosted by Professor Jeffrey J. Kripal, an expert in unusual human experiences at Rice University. His academic work focuses on events that are difficult to explain through ordinary understanding.

The miniseries also incorporates material from Rice University’s Centre for the Impossible, which is connected to the Archives of the Impossible. Viewers will get to know about telepathy, near-death experiences, UFO sightings, alleged alien abductions, prophetic dreams, and messages that people believe came from beyond.

The miniseries also features ordinary human beings who have come across unusual activities. They are mainly related to events that are hard to believe and explain.

Want to know everything about Archive X: Unexplained Phenomena? Continue reading!

Archive X: Unexplained Phenomena explores UFO encounters and alleged alien abductions

Since Archive X: Unexplained Phenomena is yet to premiere, complete details about the episodes haven't been disclosed. However, it promises to show real-world reports drawn from the Rice archives and new interviews. The miniseries includes:

Reported childhood encounters and mysterious messages: Archive X: Unexplained Phenomena will bring stories from people who encountered strange beings during childhood. Not only that, but some even thought those messages were from a very different intelligence.

Dr. John E. Mack's research: Another key part of the miniseries is Dr. John E. Mack's research. He's a Harvard psychiatrist who investigated people who claimed that they were taken away by aliens.

Dr. Mack even considered the possibility of these events because the explanations looked genuine and not something related to psychological problems that people he investigated might have. So, this becomes a key part of the miniseries because viewers will get a closer look into what the claims were about aliens abducting humans.

Whitley Strieber's reported experiences: The series also features author Whitley Strieber, who chronicled his own alleged visits in his book titled Communion. The book soon brought Strieber fame for his experiences.

Once his book was published, a lot of people sent him messages and letters, claiming that they had similar experiences. His work and claims from people added to the information regarding alien sightings and unusual events.

Connections between UFOs and spiritual experiences: Archive X: Unexplained Phenomena will also shed light on a very important question: whether there is a connection between UFO sightings and what is believed to be demonic or spiritual attacks.

Archive X: Unexplained Phenomena examines prophetic dreams and precognition

Episode 3, titled "Dark Visions," is expected to focus on a man who says he has been troubled by dreams that seem to predict events before they happen. His experiences form an important part of the episode’s exploration of precognition.

The documentary also looks at historical material about secret government programs that studied abilities such as precognition and remote viewing. These programs explored whether people could obtain information beyond what ordinary senses could provide.

Additionally, Episode 5 of the documentary will also focus on other people claiming to have seen the future. Overall, the six episodes are packed with a lot of questions, archives collected over the years, and personal experiences.
